post.summary: Give OpenVibe.Actor a task: POST /api/v1/tasks with the task in plain words, a mode (cheapest, balanced, best, fastest, private) and a budget.
post.description: **actor.task.create** (public): Give OpenVibe.Actor a task: POST /api/v1/tasks with the task in plain words, a mode (cheapest, balanced, best, fastest, private) and a budget. Actor picks the agent system for it with openvibe-sdk/placement, runs it, has a second model family check the result, and records the result, the cost to the cent and the explanation on the task (platform.task@1, answered 201 with state queued). POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/cancel stops a task that has not ended. A person's tasks are theirs; a token that names a project puts the task in that project. Each person has a daily free allowance; a task whose cheapest eligible agent would cost more than its budget fails with actor.budget.exceeded instead of running.

actor.agent-list-result.v1.title: ActorAgentListResult
actor.agent-list-result.v1.description: actor.agent-list-result@1: GET /api/v1/agents (capability actor.agent.read): every agent system Actor can route a task to. KIND is the backend class (ADR-044): openvibe-runtime (OpenVibe's own agent, acting through OpenVibe services), agent-platform (another platform's agent, called through its API), open-model (an open model on OpenVibe's own hardware), codes (coding work through OpenVibe.Codes), node and run (a person's machine or OpenVibe.Run). TRUST is ADR-046's class; private mode takes only first-party ones. CAN are the task classes and tools it takes (task:<class>, tool:<name>). RATE_CARD is the published price, revised by review and never written by a model (SOURCE says where it comes from, VERIFIED_AT when a person last checked it). AVAILABLE says whether it can take a task now and REASON why not.

per_call_usd.description: A fixed charge per tool call the platform bills (for example a web search).

actor.task-create-request.v1.title: ActorTaskCreateRequest
actor.task-create-request.v1.description: actor.task-create-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/tasks on OpenVibe.Actor (capability actor.task.create), the creation subset of platform.task@1. TASK is the instruction in plain words. MODE is the planner objective (default balanced). BUDGET caps what this task may cost (per_task_usd) and what the caller's tasks may cost in one UTC day (per_day_usd); either may be left out for the person's free-allowance defaults, and a value above the person's tier is refused 422 actor.budget.over_tier, never silently lowered. AGENT pins one agent system by its id from GET /api/v1/agents (routing still checks that it can take the task). IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat from the same requester within 24 h with an identical body answers the first task (200), with a different body 409 actor.idempotency.conflict.

agent.description: An agent system id from GET /api/v1/agents.

actor.task-list-result.v1.description: actor.task-list-result@1: GET /api/v1/tasks (capability actor.task.list): the caller's latest tasks, newest first, and NEXT, the `before` cursor for the following page (null on the last page).

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

platform.placement-result.v1.title: PlacementResult
platform.placement-result.v1.description: Where a workload was (or would be) placed and why: the chosen candidate, the reasons, and every candidate with its eligibility, estimated cost and latency (POST /api/v1/placement/explain; roadmap WS-Z9).

selected.description: The id of the chosen candidate, or null when none qualified — every candidate was ineligible or none was offered — in which case `reasons` says why. openvibe-sdk/placement plan() returns null on the same condition.

platform.task.v1.title: Task
platform.task.v1.description: platform.task@1 (plan T17, ADR-044): one task at OpenVibe.Actor's task router. POST /api/v1/tasks (actor.task.create) creates it from a plain-language `task` plus a `mode` and a `budget`; the router mints `id`, sets `state` and `created_at`, picks a backend from the registered agent systems, runs the task, verifies the result, escalates or fails over, and answers with `result`, `cost` and `explanation`. GET /api/v1/tasks/{id} (actor.task.read) reads the same resource. Progress streams as server-sent events from `progress.stream_url` (actor.task-event@1; the task's own counter in `progress.last_seq`); `cancel` records that a cancel was requested (POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/cancel), `error` says why a task failed, and `webhooks` are the registered endpoints the router delivers each state change to. Owned by `network` like every other platform.* contract and implemented by OpenVibe.Actor (manifests/services/actor.json). This v1 contract may grow optional fields.
platform.task.v1.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract. It is the task resource, not a device frame: Actor's link is HTTP/SSE where Run's is the Node WebSocket.

id.description: Minted by the router (tsk_<ULID>): the idempotency key of the task and the stem of its usage readings, as platform.job@1's id is for a job. Never reused.

project_id.description: The project the caller's token names (ADR-034 §5): budgets, usage and the bill are the project's. Absent for a person's own task (one made signed in, without a project token): the person's free allowance and daily budget apply.

requester.description: The person or agent the task belongs to: a user subject for a person, an agent subject for an agent acting under the grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2).

task.description: The instruction in plain words, exactly as the caller gave it. Not a backend command and not a model prompt: the planner turns it into one.

mode.description: The plan's five modes, in contract spelling: Cheapest, Balanced (the default), Best, Fastest and Private are `cheapest`, `balanced`, `best`, `fastest` and `private`. A mode is the planner objective, never a fixed backend list (plan T17). `cheapest`: the lowest expected cost that still meets the task class's quality bar. `balanced` (the default): cost, quality and speed weighed together. `best`: the highest chance of a right answer first time. `fastest`: the shortest time to a checked result. `private`: only backends that keep the data on OpenVibe (first-party, and a user-owned node only when the task names it), per ADR-046.

budget.description: Hard limits the router never exceeds (plan T17: 'a hard limit per task and per day'). A task whose cheapest eligible backend would take it over `per_task_usd` ends failed (actor.budget.exceeded) rather than running; `per_day_usd` caps the project's tasks in one UTC day and a new task waits or fails, it never overruns.

state.description: queued: stored, waiting for the planner. running: a backend is working, or a cascade is between attempts. verifying: a result exists and a check (the task's own tests, a citation check, a postcondition) runs before it is delivered. succeeded, failed and cancelled are the end states; an end state never changes.

finished_at.description: When the task reached its end state; null before.

result.description: The checked deliverable (any JSON, as a platform.job@1 `result` is): for a code task a diff or branch reference, for research a brief with citations, for an action a postcondition report. Never a credential and never raw sandbox output. Null (or absent) in every state but succeeded, which the allOf below enforces.

usd.description: What this task was billed, to the cent, across every attempt it made.

free_allowance_used.description: The part of `usd` covered by the project's free allowance; metered as platform.usage-sample@1.

cost.description: Present once the task has run an attempt (also when it ends failed or cancelled); null while queued. One key, one bill (plan T17), through Billing (ADR-012).

explanation.description: One platform.placement-result@1 per backend the planner tried, oldest first, an escalation appending a new one: which backend won, why and what else was considered, from openvibe-sdk/placement (ADR-046 §1). Null while queued.

stream_url.description: The text/event-stream endpoint that carries this task's progress. Each event mirrors platform.job-frame@1's job_stdout/state shape: a state change, an output chunk, or the end.

last_seq.description: The task's own event counter, from 0 before the first event; a reconnecting reader resumes after it, as a job frame's seq counts on one link.

events.description: The event kinds the stream delivers, run.job-stream-event@1's own three.

progress.description: Streaming progress (plan T17). Null before the router opens a stream and after the end.

requested_at.description: When POST /v1/tasks/{id}/cancel was accepted. The running backend is stopped as its own contract allows; the state becomes cancelled and `finished_at` is set.

cancel.description: Cancellation (plan T17): null until a cancel is requested, then it records who asked and when; the task's outcome is `state`.

url.description: The HTTPS endpoint the router POSTs a state change to. A plain-HTTP URL is refused.

events.description: The state changes delivered; the same names as `state`.

secret_ref.description: The NAME of the project secret used to sign the delivery (an HMAC header), never the secret itself, as community.moderation-request@1 names a webhook_url_ref and ADR-043 keeps device credentials by reference.

webhooks.description: Webhooks (plan T17), registered at creation. A delivery that fails is retried with backoff and never delays the task; the task's own record is the source of truth.

code.description: A stable problem code, e.g. actor.budget.exceeded, actor.no_agent, actor.check.failed, actor.task.interrupted.

error.description: Why the task failed, once it has; null otherwise. Never a credential and never raw provider output.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
